title: Attention kernel sigmoid backoff and prefill oscillation diagnostics
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Investigate recurrent oscillations observed during prefill->decode handoffs when FlashAttention v3 is preferred by the kernel selector for mixed-precision models. Hypothesis: aggressive kernel switching combined with aggressive prefill pacing causes a feedback loop (through bursty KV cache warmup and workspace fragmentation) leading to 95th/99th latency spikes. Implement a sigmoid-shaped backoff for kernel switch aggressiveness and collect telemetry to validate reduction in oscillations.
replication_steps: Roll forward a staged canary where kernel selector prefers FA3 for batches with seq_len<=1024 and quantized layout
Replay production trace (2025-02-18 03:00 UTC) on canary harness with tenant isolation and identical batching distribution
Measure 50/95/99 latency and kernel switch frequency histograms
Capture workspace allocation/deallocation counts and KV cache hit-rates per request
observations: Replayed trace shows kernel switch rate spikes around burst window boundaries (every ~4s)
KV cache hit-rate drops from 82% to 56% during oscillation windows
Workspace fragmentation increases transiently causing extra kernel allocation retries on ~0.7% of requests
Tail latency correlates with kernel switch count per request (>3 switches -> 2.3x 99th latency)
proposed_solution: Introduce sigmoid backoff curve to modulate kernel switch probability based on recent switch history and current tenant KV hit-rate
Add a temporal low-pass filter on prefill pacing decisions to avoid oscillatory readjustments within a configured damping window (default 6s)
Prefer stable kernel variant for requests with live KV cache hit-rate < 60% until a grace period elapses
Instrument new metrics: kernel_switch_backoff, prefill_damping_active, per-tenant backoff_score
experiments: A/B test: baseline selector vs selector+sigmoid-backoff on 10% of canary traffic for 48h
Stress-run: synthetic burst patterns (every 2s/4s/8s) across batch sizes 1..16 to measure hysteresis behavior
Long-run: 7-day replay with mixed tenant shapes to estimate steady state improvement
results_summary: Initial 12h canary: 27% reduction in kernel switch frequency, 18% reduction in 95th latency, 22% reduction in 99th for targeted tenants
KV hit-rate recovered to steady baseline within 8s after a burst with backoff enabled (vs ~20s baseline)
Workspace allocation retries reduced from 0.7% to 0.15% in canary
risks_and_tradeoffs: Backoff may slightly increase mean latency for cold-start single-request flows (expected +3-8ms)
Overly conservative backoff could underutilize FA3 capacity leading to cost regression for high-throughput tenants
Need to tune per-tenant thresholds to avoid one-size-fits-all pitfalls
next_steps: Merge feature-flagged sigmoid-backoff into runtime feature branch (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1427)
Add per-tenant override controls in Dedicated/Private configs and surface via Console (PM: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Kernel+Backoff+Controls)
Run a staged rollout: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with telemetry gates (kernel_switch_rate and 99th latency thresholds)
Schedule post-rollout retrospective and follow-up tuning session (owners: Aisha, Liam, Priya)
